mechanism.plausibility_rationale: Gastrointestinal hemorrhage is a plausible side effect of nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) like the one described. NSAIDs, including those that non-selectively inhibit both COX-1 and COX-2 enzymes, can lead to irritation and damage to the gastric mucosa. COX-1 is primarily responsible for the production of protective prostaglandins in the stomach lining, and inhibiting it can reduce this protection, making the stomach more susceptible to damage from acid and pepsin. This can result in ulcers, bleeding, and, in severe cases, gastrointestinal hemorrhage. Therefore, the risk of gastrointestinal hemorrhage is high with this type of NSAID.
